meta.name: Lotfollahi Lab Research Path — 12-Month Optimized
meta.target: Computational biology researcher at Wellcome Sanger Institute (Lotfollahi Lab)

weekday_breakdown.monday: Theory — paper reading, derivations, implement key equation
weekday_breakdown.tuesday: Implementation — build on Monday code, debug, visualize, commit
weekday_breakdown.wednesday: Depth — go deep on one sub-concept, reproduce specific result
weekday_breakdown.thursday: Biology (from month 4) — Scanpy workflows, Lotfollahi papers, planning
weekday_breakdown.friday: Writing + community — blog drafts, Twitter/X, week review

weekend_breakdown.saturday: Deep work block 1 (2.5 hrs): major implementation. Break (0.5 hr). Deep work block 2 (2 hrs): experiment/analysis
weekend_breakdown.sunday: Paper reading + replication (2 hrs). Blog/README writing (1.5 hrs). Week planning (0.5 hr). Light review (1 hr)

phases.name: Phase 1 — Core ML Foundations
phases.description: Build elite-level PyTorch, deep maths intuition, and GNN mastery. Deliver a VAE repo and GNN repo that would impress any ML researcher. Non-negotiable base — no computational biology without it.

topics.name: PyTorch Deep Mastery
resources: PyTorch official tutorials (pytorch.org/tutorials)
Dive into Deep Learning (d2l.ai) — Chapters 1-5

topics.name: Backpropagation & Optimization
resources: Deep Learning — Goodfellow, Bengio, Courville (Chapters 6-8)
The Matrix Calculus You Need for Deep Learning — Parr & Howard (free PDF)

topics.name: Mathematics Foundations
resources: Mathematics for Machine Learning — Deisenroth et al. (free PDF)
The Matrix Calculus You Need for Deep Learning — Parr & Howard

topics.name: Autoencoders
resources: Deep Learning — Goodfellow Chapter 14
Implement from scratch in PyTorch before using any library

topics.name: Variational Autoencoders
resources: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes — Kingma & Welling 2013 (arXiv:1312.6114) — read 10 times
Tutorial on Variational Autoencoders — Doersch 2016 (arXiv:1606.05908)
Derive ELBO by hand before implementing

topics.name: Embeddings & Representations
resources: d2l.ai Chapter 14-15
Word2Vec original papers (Mikolov et al. 2013)

topics.name: Transformers & Attention
resources: Attention Is All You Need — Vaswani et al. 2017 (arXiv:1706.03762)
The Illustrated Transformer — Jay Alammar blog post
Annotated Transformer — Harvard NLP

topics.name: Graph Convolutional Networks
resources: Semi-Supervised Classification with GCN — Kipf & Welling 2017 (arXiv:1609.02907)
CS224W Lectures 1-8 — Stanford (YouTube, free)
Implement from scratch before using PyG

topics.name: Graph Attention Networks
resources: Graph Attention Networks — Veličković et al. 2018 (arXiv:1710.10903)
CS224W Lectures 9-12

topics.name: GraphSAGE
resources: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs — Hamilton et al. 2017 (arXiv:1706.02216)

topics.name: Message Passing Neural Networks
resources: Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry — Gilmer et al. 2017 (arXiv:1704.01212)

topics.name: Convolutional Neural Networks
resources: Deep Learning — Goodfellow Chapter 9
CS231n — Stanford (notes, free online)

topics.name: Graph Transformers
resources: Do Transformers Really Perform Bad for Graph Representation? — Ying et al. 2021
Recipe for a General, Powerful, Scalable Graph Transformer — Rampasek et al. 2022

topics.name: Geometric Deep Learning
resources: Geometric Deep Learning: Grids, Groups, Graphs, Geodesics, and Gauges — Bronstein et al. 2021 (free PDF)

deliverables: MLP trained on CIFAR-10 achieving 80%+ accuracy
Autoencoder repo with MNIST latent space visualization
VAE from scratch — full repo with ELBO derivation in README
GNN from scratch repo — GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, graph AE
GitHub commit history showing steady progression

projects.name: VAE From Scratch
projects.description: Implement a complete VAE with training, visualization of latent space, and generation. Do NOT use high-level libraries — build encoder, reparameterization, decoder, ELBO loss from primitive PyTorch.

milestones.description: Basic autoencoder working on MNIST
Add variational inference: KL divergence term + reparameterization trick
Train on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, log loss curves with wandb
Latent space visualization (PCA + UMAP) and latent interpolation
Conditional VAE: condition on class labels, generate class-specific samples
README with mathematical derivation of ELBO written from scratch

projects.name: Graph Neural Networks From Scratch
projects.description: Complete GNN implementations with mathematical derivations and experiments. Implement each architecture manually before switching to PyG. Final repo should be a reference-quality resource.

milestones.description: GCN implementation + Cora node classification experiment
GAT implementation + attention visualization
GraphSAGE implementation + inductive experiment
Molecular property prediction on QM9 with MPNN
Graph autoencoder for link prediction
Clean README with math derivations, benchmark table, and learning notes

phases.name: Phase 2 — Enter Computational Biology
phases.description: Overlap with Phase 1 from month 4. Domain transition into single-cell computational biology. Learn biology through the computational lens — biology is a means to understand the data format, not an end in itself.

topics.name: Cell Biology for ML
resources: Single-cell best practices book — sc-best-practices.org (Chapters 1-3, free online)
A primer on single-cell RNA sequencing — YouTube lectures by Fabian Theis lab

topics.name: Scanpy & AnnData
subtopics: AnnData structure: obs, var, obsm, uns
resources: Scanpy PBMC tutorial (scanpy.readthedocs.io)
Scanpy paper — Wolf et al. Genome Biology 2018
AnnData documentation and tutorials

topics.name: Batch Correction Methods
resources: Benchmarking atlas-level data integration — Luecken et al. 2022
scvi-tools documentation

topics.name: Lotfollahi Papers Deep Dive
subtopics: trVAE — conditional generation with MMD loss
resources: scGen — Lotfollahi et al. Nature Methods 2019
trVAE — Lotfollahi et al. Bioinformatics 2020 (arXiv:1910.01791)
CPA — Lotfollahi et al. Nature Genetics 2023
expiMap — Lotfollahi et al. Nature Cell Biology 2023
chemCPA — Hetzel et al. 2022 (arXiv:2204.13545)

topics.name: Single-Cell ML
resources: scVI — Lopez et al. Nature Methods 2018
Geneformer — Theodoris et al. Nature 2023
scGPT — Cui et al. Nature Methods 2024
Single-cell best practices book (Chapters 4-8)

deliverables: Scanpy PBMC tutorial completed end-to-end with own annotations
scGen reproduction with comparison to paper figures
trVAE reproduction with MMD loss implemented
CPA deep dive writeup — architecture explained in own words
Single-cell VAE for perturbation prediction — original project

projects.name: scGen Reproduction
projects.description: Reproduce scGen paper results from scratch. Implement the VAE architecture independently — do not copy lab code. Document every discrepancy between your results and the paper. This is the single most important credibility signal for the lab.

milestones.description: Read paper 3 times — annotate every equation and design choice
Process Kang et al. 2018 IFN-β dataset with Scanpy
Implement VAE encoder, decoder, perturbation vector arithmetic
Train and evaluate: compare predicted vs actual stimulated cells
Write up results: what matched, what did not, and why
Publish GitHub repo with reproduction report

projects.name: trVAE Reproduction
projects.description: Reproduce trVAE — conditional generation across conditions using MMD loss. Focus on understanding the conditional architecture and the Maximum Mean Discrepancy regularization.

milestones.description: Understand MMD loss: derive it, implement it from scratch
Implement conditional encoder with condition embedding
Train on dataset from paper, evaluate conditional generation
Publish repo with clean README

projects.name: Single-cell VAE for Perturbation Prediction
projects.description: Build an original perturbation prediction system combining ideas from scGen and CPA. Make at least one architectural decision of your own. Train on a real public dataset (Replogle et al. 2022 Perturb-seq). Benchmark against scGen and CPA baselines. Treat the write-up as a mini-paper.

milestones.description: Design architecture — document every choice and rationale
Implement conditional perturbation encoding with new design element
Train on Replogle et al. 2022 Perturb-seq dataset
Benchmark against scGen and CPA baselines quantitatively
GitHub repo with documentation, demo notebook, and results table

phases.name: Phase 3 — Become Publicly Visible
phases.description: Build research identity in parallel with all other work. Associate yourself with ML for biology, generative modeling, GNNs, perturbation learning. You need to be findable before you reach out.

blogPlan.title: scGen explained — how VAEs predict perturbation responses
My scGen reproduction — what matched, what did not, and why
GNNs for single-cell biology — a practical guide
Breaking down a recent Lotfollahi lab preprint
Building a perturbation VAE from scratch — architecture decisions

phases.name: Phase 5 — Strategic Outreach
phases.description: Strategic outreach with substance. Become 'that engineering student seriously transitioning into AI biology.' Never email Mo before you have something real. Reach PhD students and postdocs first.

topics.name: Outreach Preparation
subtopics: reproduce a paper before emailing its author
prepare specific technical question from reproduction
GitHub portfolio ready before first contact
Twitter/X presence established before first contact

topics.name: PhD Student / Postdoc Outreach
subtopics: email the PhD student whose paper you reproduced
include: reproduction repo link, one specific technical question
do not ask about internships or positions in first contact
follow up once after 3 weeks if no reply
topics.emailTemplate: Subject: Reproduction of [their paper] — question on [specific technical point]. Body: I reproduced [paper] and trained it on [dataset]. I found [specific observation]. I am trying to understand [specific question]. Link to repo: [GitHub link]. Would you be open to a brief async exchange? (~3 sentences max)

topics.name: Mo Lotfollahi Outreach
subtopics: email only after: scGen reproduction, CPA study, perturbation VAE project
link to GitHub — not a CV attachment
state one specific research question you want to explore
ask for collaboration or small project — not a position
one follow-up after 3 weeks if no reply
topics.emailTemplate: Subject: Implementation of CPA + proposed extension for [specific thing]. Body (150 words max): I am a final-year CE student who reproduced scGen and studied CPA in detail. I built [perturbation VAE project name] — [one sentence on what it does]. GitHub: [link]. I noticed [specific technical observation from your reproduction]. I am curious whether [specific research question]. Is there room for a remote collaboration or small project? I can commit [X hours per week].

topics.name: Remote Research Collaboration
subtopics: PhD program applications: Cambridge, ETH Zurich, EMBL

deliverables: Outreach to 2-3 lab PhD students with reproduction repo links
Email to Mo Lotfollahi with substance — GitHub link, specific question
Formal applications to Sanger / Open Targets / EMBL-EBI programs

monthly_milestones.title: PyTorch foundation
goals: Complete PyTorch official tutorials end-to-end
Implement linear regression, MLP, and CNN from scratch using only raw PyTorch
Master autograd: compute gradients manually on paper, then verify with PyTorch
Build a custom Dataset + DataLoader for a real dataset (not MNIST)
Read Goodfellow Chapters 6-8 (backprop, regularization, optimization)
Read The Matrix Calculus You Need for Deep Learning — Parr & Howard
monthly_milestones.deliverable: Working MLP trained on CIFAR-10 with 80%+ accuracy — committed to GitHub

monthly_milestones.title: Optimization + Autoencoders
goals: Implement SGD, Adam, RMSprop from scratch — verify outputs match PyTorch
Understand learning rate scheduling: cosine annealing, step decay, linear warmup
Build a basic autoencoder for MNIST — visualize latent space with PCA and UMAP
Implement denoising autoencoder — understand noise injection and reconstruction
Derive KL divergence from scratch on paper: know it by heart
Implement batch normalization from scratch
monthly_milestones.deliverable: Autoencoder GitHub repo with latent space visualization notebook

monthly_milestones.title: VAE mastery
goals: Read Kingma & Welling 2013 VAE paper — minimum 3 full passes with annotations
Derive ELBO by hand from the definition of the marginal likelihood
Implement VAE: encoder, reparameterization trick, decoder, combined ELBO loss
Train on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST — visualize latent traversals and interpolations
Implement beta-VAE and observe disentanglement effect
Implement Conditional VAE — condition on class labels
monthly_milestones.deliverable: vae-from-scratch GitHub repo with ELBO derivation written in README

monthly_milestones.title: GNNs begin + Biology entry
goals: Study spectral graph theory: graph Laplacian, eigendecomposition, spectral convolution
Read and implement GCN (Kipf & Welling 2017) from adjacency matrix up
Watch CS224W Lectures 1-8 (Stanford, YouTube)
Install Scanpy — complete the PBMC3k tutorial end-to-end with own annotations
Learn AnnData structure cold: obs, var, obsm, obsp, uns
Read single-cell best practices book Chapters 1-2
Begin biology self-study: central dogma, RNA, gene expression
monthly_milestones.deliverable: GCN for Cora node classification committed to GitHub + Scanpy PBMC tutorial completed

monthly_milestones.title: GAT + scGen entry + public presence
goals: Implement GAT from scratch — attention over neighbors, multi-head version
Implement GraphSAGE — inductive learning, neighborhood sampling, aggregation functions
Read scGen paper (Lotfollahi et al. Nature Methods 2019) in full — annotate every equation
Process Kang et al. 2018 IFN-β dataset with Scanpy
Understand scGen architecture: what does the perturbation vector arithmetic mean biologically?
Begin scGen implementation — encoder, latent perturbation, decoder
Start Twitter/X presence: post first progress thread showing your VAE visualization
monthly_milestones.deliverable: GAT implementation on GitHub + first Twitter/X thread posted

monthly_milestones.title: GNN project complete + scGen reproduce
goals: Complete GNN-from-scratch repo: GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, MPNN, graph AE
Write comprehensive README with mathematical derivations for each architecture
Complete scGen reproduction: train, apply perturbation arithmetic, evaluate
Compare your scGen results to paper figures — document every discrepancy
Read trVAE paper — understand MMD loss and the conditional generation setup
Begin trVAE implementation
Begin blog post 1: 'scGen explained — how VAEs predict perturbation responses'
monthly_milestones.deliverable: scGen reproduction repo on GitHub with reproduction report

monthly_milestones.title: CPA deep dive + first PhD student outreach
goals: Complete trVAE reproduction
Read CPA paper (Lotfollahi et al. Nature Genetics 2023) in detail — 3 full passes
Study CPA architecture: how does embedding arithmetic for drugs and genes work?
Begin CPA implementation from scratch (expect this to take 4-6 weeks)
Publish blog post 1 on Medium or personal site
Email 1-2 PhD students in the Lotfollahi lab with your scGen reproduction repo
monthly_milestones.deliverable: Blog post 1 published + first outreach email sent with GitHub link

monthly_milestones.title: CPA complete + specialization decision
goals: Complete CPA reproduction — evaluate on held-out perturbations
Map the full Lotfollahi lab ecosystem: all papers, co-authors, GitHub repos, connections to Theis lab
Choose specialization track: Generative models for perturbation OR GNNs for spatial transcriptomics
For spatial track: install Squidpy, read Visium data format, build first tissue graph
For generative track: read diffusion models paper, understand flow matching
Publish blog post 2: 'CPA explained — compositional perturbation autoencoder'
Find first scvi-tools good-first-issue and start work
monthly_milestones.deliverable: Specialization track committed + scvi-tools issue filed or PR opened

monthly_milestones.title: Perturbation VAE + Mo outreach
goals: Build original perturbation VAE combining scGen + CPA ideas with at least one novel design choice
Implement conditional perturbation encoding on Replogle et al. 2022 Perturb-seq data
Begin quantitative benchmarking against scGen and CPA baselines
Submit first PR to scvi-tools
Publish blog post 3: 'My scGen reproduction — findings and discrepancies'
Email Mo Lotfollahi — 150 words, GitHub link, specific research question
monthly_milestones.deliverable: Perturbation VAE repo started + Mo Lotfollahi email sent

monthly_milestones.title: Polish + open source contribution
goals: Respond to any feedback from Lotfollahi lab contacts
Complete perturbation VAE project: benchmarking, documentation, demo notebook
Clean all GitHub repos: consistent structure, requirements.txt, demo notebooks
Get scvi-tools PR reviewed and merged
Apply to: Wellcome Sanger Research Engineer, Open Targets, EMBL-EBI programs
Publish blog post 4: 'GNNs for single-cell biology — a practical guide'
Aim for 10+ substantive conversations with researchers on Twitter/X
monthly_milestones.deliverable: First open-source PR merged + formal program applications submitted

monthly_milestones.title: Depth + second project
goals: Go deeper on chosen specialization — read 5 additional papers in the sub-area
Start a second original project or a meaningful extension of month 9 project
Prepare a 5-slide research summary deck for potential interviews
Publish blog post 5: breakdown of a very recent Lotfollahi lab preprint
Follow up on any open applications
Engage in at least one substantive comp-bio discussion per week on Twitter/X
monthly_milestones.deliverable: Second project started + research summary deck ready

monthly_milestones.title: Final push + position
goals: Complete second project and GitHub repo
Finalize portfolio: 6+ repos, 4+ blog posts, 1+ open-source contributions merged
Write a 1-page personal research statement: what problem do you want to solve and why?
Apply to remaining programs or research engineer positions
Final follow-up to Lotfollahi if no response received
Explore PhD program applications for 2026 entry: Cambridge, ETH Zurich, EMBL-EBI
monthly_milestones.deliverable: Full portfolio live + all formal applications submitted

anti_patterns: Do not email Mo Lotfollahi before month 9 unless you have exceptional output to show
Do not say 'I am very interested in your research' — every email says this
Do not ask for a PhD position — ask for a collaboration or small defined project
Do not send a CV attachment in the first email — link your GitHub instead
Do not start CPA implementation before finishing scGen reproduction
Do not use scGen lab code to reproduce scGen — implement from the paper
Do not disappear from Twitter/X between milestone completions — consistency matters
Do not learn Scanpy before having PyTorch and VAE foundations solid
Do not copy-paste implementations — type every line and understand every parameter
